subject: comprehensive-regulatory-crosswalks-csoai22
honest_sentence: Comprehensive crosswalks: 11 regulations × 22 CSOAI axes, COBOLBridge positioning, insurance risk pricing, and token release measurement. Maps compliance requirements to measurement axes — never claims certification.

CLARITY_Act.status: cloture vote Sep 15 2026; 15-16% Polymarket for 2026 enactment
key_provisions: Digital commodity classification (CFTC jurisdiction for non-securities)
SEC retains jurisdiction over investment-contract tokens
Stablecoin issuer registration and reserve requirements
Exchange/broker registration: Day 180/270/540 implementation cliffs
360-day all-rules mandate post-enactment
Ethics sunset Jan 2029

A22_x402: Machine-native payment rails for compliance attestations

GENIUS_Act.status: signed into law; 129 days until mandatory monthly PCAOB-disclosed attestations
key_provisions: Payment stablecoin definition (1:1 reserve, <1yr T-bills or insured deposits)
Monthly PCAOB-examined, CEO/CFO-certified disclosures
Issuer reserve segregation and prohibition on rehypothecation
Federal and state dual charter path (OCC/FDIC/state regulators)
Prohibition on algorithmic-only stablecoins without full reserve
Rulemaking deadline already missed; OCC targeting Nov 2026

EU_AI_Act.status: in force; Annex III high-risk obligations phasing in through Aug 2027
EU_AI_Act.jurisdiction: EU (extraterritorial for providers placing AI in EU market)
key_provisions: Art 5: Prohibited AI practices (social scoring, real-time biometric, subliminal manipulation)
Art 50: Transparency obligations (chatbot disclosure, deepfake marking, emotion recognition notice)
Art 6/Annex III: High-risk AI systems in 8 domains (biometrics, critical infra, education, employment, law enforcement, migration, justice, democracy)
Art 55: General-purpose AI model obligations (transparency, copyright, systemic risk)
Art 113: Implementation timeline (prohibited = Feb 2025, GPAI = Aug 2025, high-risk = Aug 2027)

A7_fairness: Art 10 data governance for bias prevention
A13_impact: Art 55 systemic risk assessment for GPAI
A17_ISO42001: ISO 42001 as harmonised standard under Art 40
A19_IEEE: IEEE 7000 series for ethical AI design

GDPR.status: in force since 2018; AI-specific enforcement intensifying (DPA guidance on AI 2025-2026)
GDPR.jurisdiction: EU/EEA (extraterritorial: any entity processing EU personal data)
key_provisions: Art 5: Data processing principles (lawfulness, purpose limitation, minimisation)
Art 6/9: Lawful basis and special categories
Art 13-14: Information obligations (including automated decision-making disclosures)
Art 22: Automated individual decision-making (right not to be subject to solely automated decisions)
Art 25: Data protection by design and default
Art 35: DPIA for high-risk processing (AI training/inference on personal data)
Art 44-49: International transfers (Schrems III implications for AI cloud)

A13_impact: Art 36 prior consultation for residual high risk

DORA.status: in force since Jan 2025; ICT risk management and TLO oversight operational
DORA.jurisdiction: EU financial entities and their ICT third-party providers
key_provisions: Art 5-16: ICT risk management framework (governance, strategy, detection, response)
Art 17-23: ICT-related incident reporting (classification, timelines, harmonised templates)
Art 24-27: Digital operational resilience testing (TLPT for significant entities)
Art 28-44: ICT third-party risk management (contractual arrangements, exit strategies)
Art 45-48: Oversight framework for critical ICT third-party providers

A1_governance: Art 5-6 management body accountability for ICT risk

NIS2.status: in force since Oct 2024; member state transposition ongoing
NIS2.jurisdiction: EU essential and important entities across 18 sectors
key_provisions: Art 21: Cybersecurity risk management measures (risk analysis, incident handling, BC/DR)
Art 20: Governance and management body liability
Art 23: Incident reporting (24h early warning, 72h notification, 1 month final report)
Art 22: Cybersecurity audit obligations
Art 25: Supply chain security
Art 27: Peer review mechanism

Cyber_Resilience_Act.status: vulnerability reporting obligations started Sep 11 2026; full application Sep 2027
Cyber_Resilience_Act.jurisdiction: EU (manufacturers, importers, distributors of products with digital elements)
key_provisions: Art 6-7: Essential cybersecurity requirements (secure by design, vulnerability handling)
Art 11-13: Vulnerability handling and coordinated disclosure obligations
Art 14: SBOM (software bill of materials) obligations
Art 35-51: Conformity assessment procedures
Art 67: Market surveillance and enforcement

A2_safety: No known exploitable vulnerabilities at delivery
A18_OWASP: OWASP Top 10 alignment for digital products

MiCA.status: in force since Jun 2024; stablecoin provisions active, CASP licensing phased
MiCA.jurisdiction: EU crypto-asset service providers and token issuers
key_provisions: Title II: General crypto-asset issuance (white paper requirements, marketing rules)
Title III: Asset-referenced tokens (reserve, governance, redemption rights)
Title IV: E-money tokens (1:1 redemption, reserve in same-currency deposits/low-risk assets)
Title V-IV: CASP authorization and conduct rules (exchange, custody, transfer, advice)
Title VI: Market abuse prevention (insider trading, manipulation)
Art 94-104: Supervisory and enforcement framework

A8_accountability: CASP liability for client asset loss
A13_impact: Significant ART/EMT designation (2M+ holders or 5B+ outstanding)

ISO_27001_2022.jurisdiction: Global (voluntary, widely required by enterprise customers)
key_provisions: Annex A: 93 controls in 4 themes (organisational, people, physical, technological)
Clauses 4-10: ISMS requirements (context, leadership, planning, support, operation, evaluation, improvement)
Risk-based approach to information security management
Statement of Applicability (SoA) for control selection

A4_continuity: A.5.30 ICT readiness for business continuity
A10_privacy: A.5.34 Privacy and protection of PII
A17_ISO42001: Complementary: ISO 42001 extends ISMS to AI-specific governance

SOC2_Type_II.status: ongoing; annual audits with 6-12 month observation periods
SOC2_Type_II.jurisdiction: US (voluntary, required by enterprise SaaS/cloud customers)
key_provisions: Trust Services Criteria: Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, Privacy
17 common criteria (CC1-CC9) across control environment, communication, risk, monitoring, control activities
Type I = design effectiveness at a point in time; Type II = operating effectiveness over period
Complementary user entity controls (CUECs) for shared responsibility

A1_governance: CC1 Control Environment (integrity, oversight, structure, authority)
A17_ISO42001: Complementary: ISO 42001 AI governance extends SOC2 scope to AI systems

CBDC_Monitoring.status: active monitoring: ECB Pontes pilot (2025), digital yuan (live), digital pound (design), FedNow (live since 2023)
CBDC_Monitoring.jurisdiction: global central bank digital currency programmes
key_provisions: ECB Pontes: wholesale settlement pilot, T2 replacement, tokenised deposits interaction
PBOC digital yuan (e-CNY): m-CBDC Bridge with BIS, retail + wholesale
Bank of England digital pound: design phase, primary legislation required
US: no CBDC legislation; FedNow instant payments as alternative
BIS Innovation Hub: Project mBridge (cross-border), Project Agorá (tokenised deposits + CBDC)
ISO 20022 alignment: all CBDC projects adopting ISO 20022 messaging standards

A4_continuity: Financial system continuity during CBDC transition
A8_accountability: Central bank accountability for monetary operations

market_reality.cobol_codebase_estimate: 220 billion lines of COBOL in production
market_reality.banks_on_cobol: 43 of the top 50 US banks, all major UK clearing banks, SWIFT network core
market_reality.annual_maintenance_cost: $3-5 per line of COBOL code per year globally

positioning.strategic_angle: COBOL-to-modern-bridge is the largest unaddressed IT services market in financial services
positioning.revenue_opportunity: Conservative: $2-5B addressable for measurement-driven modernization consulting
positioning.competitive_moat: Measurement-based risk scoring for legacy-to-modern migration projects (no competitor does this)

tier_1_discovery.name: Legacy System Risk Assessment
tier_1_discovery.scope: Map COBOL dependencies, measure technical debt, score modernization readiness
tier_1_discovery.deliverable: Signed measurement card per legacy system with 22-axis score

tier_2_bridge.name: Migration Risk Scoring
tier_2_bridge.deliverable: Daily signed measurement cards tracking migration risk trajectory

tier_3_trust.name: Post-Migration Trust Attestation
tier_3_trust.scope: Independent verification that migrated systems maintain equivalent integrity
tier_3_trust.deliverable: Signed trust attestation card (like SOC2 but for migration integrity)

buyer_profiles.pain: Regulatory pressure to modernize core banking; COBOL skills shortage; DORA operational resilience mandates
CBDC integration requires modern APIs; COBOL core incompatible with programmable money
ISO 20022 migration requires modern message handling; COBOL parsers are bottleneck
DORA compliance for legacy systems; risk models running on COBOL

regulatory_drivers.DORA: Art 5-16 ICT risk management requires modern monitoring — COBOL systems can't be instrumented
regulatory_drivers.NIS2: Art 21 cybersecurity measures — COBOL systems lack modern security controls
regulatory_drivers.EU_CRA: Art 6 secure-by-design — legacy COBOL impossible to retrofit
regulatory_drivers.Basel_III_4: Operational resilience requirements demand real-time risk visibility

A1_governance: Modern governance design for migrated systems

market_context.crypto_insurance_market: $2-4B gross written premium (2025 estimate); growing 40% YoY
market_context.coverage_gaps: Standard cyber policies exclude crypto custody, smart contract failure, bridge exploits
market_context.current_pricing: Ad hoc; Lloy's syndicates, Evertas, Coincover, Nexus Mutual
market_context.pain_point: No standardized risk measurement → opaque pricing, coverage denials, claims disputes

csoai_insurance_play.positioning: CSOAI provides the independent measurement substrate that makes crypto insurance insurable
csoai_insurance_play.mechanism: Signed measurement cards serve as actuarial inputs — standardized, auditable, tamper-proof risk scores
csoai_insurance_play.value_chain_position: Risk data provider to insurers (not an insurer itself — maintains neutrality)

stablecoin_risk_score.description: Per-stablecoin risk assessment using reserve quality, attestation cadence, regulatory status
stablecoin_risk_score.output: 0-100 risk score per stablecoin, updated daily, signed
stablecoin_risk_score.insurer_use: Base rate calculation for custody/reserve coverage
stablecoin_risk_score.price_to_insurer: 0.01-0.05% of gross written premium per stablecoin scored

custody_risk_score.description: Custodian operational risk based on security posture, key management, insurance coverage
custody_risk_score.output: 0-100 custody risk score per platform, signed
custody_risk_score.price_to_insurer: 0.02-0.08% of coverage amount per custodian scored

bridge_protocol_risk.description: Cross-chain bridge exploit probability based on code audit, TVL concentration, incident history
bridge_protocol_risk.output: Bridge risk score with exploit probability estimate
bridge_protocol_risk.price_to_insurer: 0.1-0.5% of coverage amount per bridge scored

exchange_operational_risk.description: Exchange solvency and operational risk scoring using proof-of-reserves, regulatory status, withdrawal patterns
exchange_operational_risk.output: Exchange solvency risk score, signed, updated weekly
exchange_operational_risk.price_to_insurer: 0.05-0.15% of coverage volume per exchange scored

total_addressable_market.adjacent_revenue: $50-200M ARR (consulting to insurers on crypto risk models)
total_addressable_market.timeline: 12-24 months to first insurer pilot; 36 months to scale
total_addressable_market.competitive_advantage: Zero competitors providing signed, daily, public crypto risk scores usable as actuarial inputs

token_release_measurement.description: Corrections-ledger methodology for measuring token releases, unlocks, and vesting schedules

market_need.problem: Token unlock schedules are opaque, scattered across vesting contracts, and frequently misrepresented by projects
market_need.impact: Billions in sell pressure invisible to market participants; insider vesting often misrepresented or undisclosed
market_need.current_state: TokenUnlocks, CryptoRank, Nansen provide partial data; no signed, auditable, correction-tracked measurement exists

csoai_approach.methodology: On-chain vesting contract monitoring → signed measurement cards → corrections ledger for any data revisions

corrections_ledger.format: JSON array of {claim, actual, error_factor, source, correction_date}

example_entries.claim: Project X unlock = 50M tokens on Sep 1

example_entries.actual: Team allocation already 73% transferred to exchange deposit wallets

correction_rules: Every data point has a claim date and source
Each correction signed with same Ed25519 key as measurement cards
Corrections are first-class evidence, not errors

A3_provenance: Token origin and vesting contract provenance
A5_soundness: Vesting schedule integrity (no early unlock without disclosure)

token_unlock_tracker.scope: Top 200 tokens by market cap; daily unlock monitoring
token_unlock_tracker.output: Signed measurement card per token per unlock event
token_unlock_tracker.price: Free public index; $500-2000/month for API access with corrections feed

insider_flow_alerts.scope: Real-time alerts when team/treasury wallets move to exchanges
insider_flow_alerts.output: Signed alert card with on-chain proof

vesting_audit.scope: Full vesting schedule reconstruction from deploy transaction to present
vesting_audit.output: Signed audit card with complete corrections ledger

token_release_measurement.total_addressable_market: $10-38M ARR for token release measurement alone
token_release_measurement.integration_with_insurance: Vesting audit scores feed directly into exchange_operational_risk insurance pricing — projects with opaque vesting get higher risk premiums
token_release_measurement.corrections_as_moat: The corrections ledger IS the moat — competitors publish data, CSOAI publishes data AND its own corrections history. Self-correcting measurement is provably more trustworthy.
